verdicts.flaw_description: The outcome measure covers units that were only partly on the new bearing: "Hours cover every bearing position on each machine, and about a third of each machine's positions had spells on the old bearing." So roughly a third of the measured positions were running the old design for part of the cycle, and the 260-410 extra hours cannot be attributed to the redesigned bearing alone.

A named alternative cause reaches every block: "Rainfall in each block's season ran about a fifth above the year before, and every block lay in open ground, under no cover." A 20 percent wetter season on uncovered maize would raise yield by itself, so the 0.4-0.7 t/ha gains are not attributable to the drip line.

Two of the four cases have follow-up dates that precede the start date: case one "started 4 March, had 6 fewer attacks by 28 February" and case three "started 5 September, had 7 fewer attacks by 30 August." The reductions are recorded before the inhaler was started, so those cases cannot be evidence of its effect (the quarter labels, e.g. "winter quarter" for a 4 March start, are likewise inconsistent).

The measured population is broader than the treated one: "Retention figures cover every signup, email opened or not, and a third of each cohort's signups never opened it." A third of each cohort was never actually exposed to the email, so the 3-6 point retention lift is measured on a population one-third of which received no treatment.

A competing cause reaches every logged class: "Class sizes at each school ran about a quarter below the year before, and every logged class took its English lessons as one whole group." Classes 25 percent smaller during whole-group English instruction could produce the 5-9 point comprehension gain on their own, independent of the reading program.

The reported rates cover a narrower population than the baseline they are compared with: "Rates cover the boards soldered on the new profile throughout, and about a tenth of each run's boards took one pass on the old profile." Roughly 10 percent of each run's boards are dropped from the new-profile figure while the "same line a month earlier" comparison covers all boards, so the 4-7 percent defect drop could come from that selection rather than the profile.
